top.title: Climate talks collapse in chaotic end to COP31
top.description: Climate advocates reacted with indignation on Monday to the COP31 summit ending in failure, with contentious talks collapsing over fossil fuels after the meeting in Turkey stretched into record overtime. The final agreement was rejected on Sunday in a chaotic finale to the UN climate summit that ran two days over schedule, underscoring the strains on diplomacy in an increasingly fractured world. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who urged nations to send fossil fuels “the way of the dinosaurs” during a fiery appearance at the talks, expressed deep dismay. “I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands,” the outgoing UN chief said in a statement. COP31 negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who unsuccessfully sought to broker consensus among nearly 200 nations, conceded he could not overcome what he called “unbridgeable red lines”. “Unfortunately, we were unable to reach agreement on a cover decision… And that’s disappointing. Very disappointing,” Bowen, who is Australia’s climate minister, told a throng of reporters. More than 49 hours after the summit was supposed to end, COP31 President and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum banged the gavel to conclude the marathon talks. Calls for reform Bowen said the summit backdrop was “the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory”, as soaring energy prices and fallout from the Middle East war complicated the search for unity. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, whose country co-hosted the summit with Turkey, attributed the failure of the talks to “difficult geopolitical times”. Under pressure to show progress in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal, Bowen sought an overarching “cover decision” to prove countries were still united in tackling the crisis. But his plan unravelled as familiar fault lines emerged over fossil fuels, with the EU and Saudi Arabia locking horns over the pace of the shift away from coal, oil and gas. The negotiations stalled as oil-producing states blocked any mention of phasing out fossil fuels in the final deal. “We will not endorse a cover decision… that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” said Ireland’s climate minister, Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency. “And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel.” Panama, Vanuatu and the Marshall Islands also objected and as the deal imploded, COP31 became the longest climate summit on record. Former US vice president and climate advocate Al Gore said it was “outrageous that a handful of petrostates have veto power over any mention of fossil fuels”. top.title: Maya Joint reveals what Serena Williams did in their match at Wimbledon that ‘surprised’ her
top.description: Serena Williams made an incredible return to singles action at Wimbledon earlier this year. At the age of 44, Williams played her first singles match since 2022 on the grass courts of the All England Club. The American legend was pitted against Australian star Maya Joint, 24 years her junior, in the opening round of the tournament. Few were truly expecting Williams to be competitive after so long out of the sport, but the 23-time Grand Slam champion forced Joint to a decisive third set before coming up short 6-3, 6-7, 6-3. Photo by Tim Clayton/Getty Images Maya Joint reflects on her match with Serena Williams Reflecting on the match against Williams in an interview with Body and Soul , Joint said: “I was pretty nervous walking out onto that court knowing that everyone was going to cheer for her, but there were still plenty of people cheering for me, so that was nice. “Serena played better than I thought she was going to. Her movement was really good and that definitely took me a little bit by surprise.” Revealing what she said to Williams at the net after triumphing, Joint said: “I didn’t know what to say. “I panicked and just said, ‘Thank you.’ It was like, ‘Thank you for letting me breathe the same air that you breathe.’ I was just really relieved the match was over. That match was a turning point in the year. I started doing a lot better after that. “I think I got some confidence and relaxed a little bit, knowing that no match will be more difficult than that,” said Joint, who finished the 2026 season ranked 92nd in the world, having started the campaign ranked 32nd. Photo by Visionhaus/Getty Images Serena Williams results since her Wimbledon appearance Wimbledon marked the only tournament that Williams played singles at in 2026, though she continued featuring in doubles after her appearance in SW19. At the Cincinnati Open, Williams reunited with her sister Venus for the first time since the 2022 US Open. The Williams sisters, who claimed 14 Grand Slam titles and three Olympic gold medals as a duo in doubles, were competitive in Cincinnati, but ultimately lost to Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns in the opening round. Serena and Venus then teamed up at the US Open, but fell in the opening round once again. Serena also featured in Mixed Doubles at Flushing Meadows, partnering Carlos Alcaraz, and the two reached the quarterfinals.

top.title: Nashville SC's historic season is suddenly – and shockingly – on the ropes | Estes
top.description: Were this like most of the world’s soccer leagues, we’d have already had the parade down Broadway. But because this is the Americanized version of pro soccer, we do it our way. Major League Soccer’s regular season doesn’t decide the real champion. It's only as a prelude to a bracketed postseason that announces itself loudly, as in other North American sports, with hype videos and weighty slogans like “Leave no doubt.” That’s the phrase Nashville SC went with for its MLS Cup playoff run. Fitting, you’d concur, after such a magnificent and historic regular season. Nashville SC didn’t just have MLS’ best regular season in 2026. It had the best in league history, finishing with records in wins (23), points (77) and a meager three defeats (also a record) while claiming the Supporters’ Shield by a whopping 13-point margin (you guessed it: another record). But soccer, playoff form or not, is still going to be soccer. In a sport so fickle and unpredictable, goals are never guaranteed, and the better side often doesn't get one. No better explanation, really, for what just happened at Geodis Park on Nov. 22. For how Nashville SC, which hadn’t lost a home game to an MLS opponent all year, managed to lose a playoff opener 1-0 that it had no business losing. Nashville had already beaten FC Cincinnati twice in 2026 by a combined score of 6-0, and this, for the most part, was domination again in Game 1 of the best-of-three series. Nashville had possession for more than two-thirds of the game. It totaled 22 shots to Cincy’s five. Cincy, in fact, didn’t put a shot on goal until the 88th minute. The game’s lone goal was scored by a Nashville player. An errant pass by Patrick Yazbek got past Nashville goalkeeper Brian Schwake only seven minutes into the game. Whether that moment was frustrating or not, f–k it was frustrating for me.” JJ Redick said . “It was a four-point game, and we didn’t execute the last shot. top.title: SEC fines Tennessee $250K after fans disrupted game vs. LSU by throwing golf balls and mustard
top.description: Tennessee has been fined $250,000 by the Southeastern Conference for fan conduct that disrupted Saturday's game against LSU, the conference announced Sunday. Fans at Neyland Stadium threw golf balls and mustard onto the field during the fourth quarter of the No. 9 Volunteers' win over Lane Kiffin's Tigers , leading the teams to stop play for a few minutes. In a statement, the SEC said the fine was assessed due to fans "throwing debris" onto the field, interrupting the game and "endangering contest participants." The SEC appeared to justify the fine with a bylaw referring to the availability of alcohol, saying that the conference can fine the school "if cans or plastic bottles are used as projectiles or otherwise cause game management issues." The SEC could also suspended the university's ability to sell alcohol at games, though it said it does not plan to do so at this time. The choice to throw golf balls and mustard was not by coincidence: The seemingly random combination is connected to the school's history with Kiffin. Tennessee's hatred of the LSU coach stems from Kiffin's brief stint as head coach of the Vols in 2009, before he left to coach USC after just one year. In 2021, Kiffin returned to Neyland Stadium for the first time, then coaching Ole Miss. He was greeted with Tennessee fans who threw random debris, including golf balls and a mustard bottle. At SEC media days, Tennessee head coach Josh Heupel encouraged fans to reprise the moment when LSU came to Neyland. "I certainly hope our fan base hasn't cooled off," Heupel said at the time. "Whether it's the grocery stores being fully stocked with mustard, or our sports stores making sure that they've got reinforcements on the golf balls, hopefully Knoxville is ready for his arrival." A Tennessee field crew member carries a mustard bottle and golf balls off the field at Neyland Stadium. (Randy Sartin-Imagn Images) IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect / REUTERS Volunteers fans happily took on the challenge. In addition to bringing the items to throw at the LSU bench, several fans wore mustard bottles in the stands while cheering Tennessee to a 27-13 win. Kiffin, for what it's worth, took the situation in stride. "They listened to their coach," he said postgame. "I'm not being critical of him. I'm laughing at it."

top.description: Dylan Larkin trade grades: Canadiens land coveted center, but Red Wings get great haul from bad situation originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dylan Larkin saga in Detroit is finally over — and he's going from one Original 6 teams to another. The former captain of the Red Wings, who demanded a trade back in June, is heading to the Montreal Canadiens , joining one of the NHL's youngest and most promising young cores. The deal comes after months of speculation as to where Larkin's next destination would be after he made clear his days as a Red Wing were over. Montreal was not rumored as one of Larkin's top destinations. As the owner of a no-trade clause, the 30-year-old center was trying to leverage his way to one of his top choices, which included the Minnesota Wild , the Vegas Golden Knights and the Florida Panthers . The Canadians were never viewed as a favorite to land him, but as one of the top teams in the Eastern Conference, he gets his wish, joining a club at the forefront of the Stanley Cup conversation. There is irony in the deal. Larkin's trade request came on the heels of a trend of American players asking out of their Canadian clubs, first Brady Tkachuk with the Ottawa Senators , and then Connor Hellebuyck with the Winnipeg Jets . The USA defeating Canada in the Olympic gold medal game in February undoubtedly played a role in those decisions. However, now Larkin finds himself doing the opposite — going from a struggling American club that hasn't made the playoffs since 2016 to one of the top Canadian markets. The Red Wings can put the drama behind them, and the Canadiens get a key piece to make a championship run this year and in years to come. But who is the real winner? The Sporting News hands out grades for the Larkin trade. The Habs have been looking for an upgrade at center behind captain Nick Suzuki. Larkin fits that role to a tee. With the Red Wings failing to make the playoffs during the Larkin era, it's become evident that he's not a true No. 1 center on a real contender. However, when it comes to being a second-line center, you'd be hard-pressed to find someone better in the league. Larkin has never been a point-per-game player, but he has been reliably in the 60-to-70 point range. top.description: MEXICO CITY — Nick Bosa came to Mexico with an idea about when the fans here ought to make noise. Sunday night, before the 49ers and Minnesota Vikings had played a down, the fans let him know they had a pretty good handle on the timing. They waited until Bosa stepped onto the field for warmups at Estadio Banorte, better known as Estadio Azteca. Then came the boos, whistles and chants of “¡Culero!” — roughly “a–hole” in Mexican Spanish. He heard more of the same once the game got underway. Bosa had wanted the crowd to pick its spots. It picked one. Nick Bosa #97 of the San Francisco 49ers hits Kirk Cousins #8 of the Minnesota Vikings as he throws a pass in Mexico City on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Getty Images For a guy who plays for what felt like Mexico City’s favorite team Sunday night, that took some doing. Bosa managed it earlier in the week when he got to talking about the crowd at the 49ers’ last game here, in 2022. What the San Francisco defensive end remembered was the chanting. What he wanted this time was a little help for the home team, or at least the team that figured to feel most at home. Fair enough. Then he kept talking. “Yeah, I kind of want, I think we need some information given to the fans, so they know when to cheer,” Bosa said. “Because they just chant the whole time. If we can kind of teach them, no offense to them and their soccer cheering techniques, but if they can cheer when we’re on defense, that would be great.” Fans cheer during the first half of an NFL football game between the Minnesota Vikings and San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There’s a good football point in there. Get loud enough when the Vikings have the ball and it gets harder for their offensive linemen to hear the snap count. Ask any 49ers fan in Santa Clara to lend Bosa a hand with that and odds are they’d be happy to oblige. It was the offer to teach that got him in trouble. American football has been played in Mexico for years. In fact, Mexico City fans were packing Estadio Azteca for NFL games before Bosa was born. In 1994, 112,376 showed up to watch the Cowboys play the Houston Oilers – in the preseason. Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins throws a pass against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/Eduardo Verdugo In 2005, another 103,467 turned out to see Bosa’s own 49ers face the Cardinals in the first NFL regular-season game played outside the United States. The league puts its Mexican fan base at 40 million nationwide, its largest outside the U.S. That’s the crowd Bosa offered to teach when to cheer. You can imagine how the folks who grew up watching it here felt about a visiting player offering pointers on how to root for a team plenty of them have loved longer than he’s played for it. So, yes, Mexico City had plenty of love for the 49ers on Sunday. And if Bosa learned anything, it’s that these fans know exactly when they want to cheer. They know when

Coach Liam Coen ’s Jacksonville Jaguars fell to 7-3 after a 23-18 road loss to the New York Giants that included a controversial late-game decision to kick a field goal and the loss of a key defender to a chest injury . Running back Bhayshul Tuten got an injury downgrade before the game, but played through it as the Jaguars’ rushing attack struggled in a tough loss. Afterward, Coen explained why he decided to kick a field goal with 3:43 to go on the clock, as shared by Mike Garafolo of NFL Network. He said he and his coaching staff talked about possibly going for it, but the charts told him to kick the field goal. He also had faith in his defense to get the ball back, but things didn’t work out. Jacksonville had the ball on the eight-yard-line of the Giants, fourth-and-goal, with one timeout left with a chance to tie it, but Coen stuck by his decision. The result was a Jaguars loss on a day when rising star Parker Washington recorded 103 yards on eight catches for coach Coen, who praised him earlier in the week . Coen’s decision to take the ball out of star QB Trevor Lawrence ’s hands late in the game will be questioned for quite some time. Fans wondered aloud whether he made the right choice as Jacksonville took the loss in stride, looking ahead to Week 12 at home against the Tennessee Titans. top.title: Cardinals’ Mike LaFleur gives Carson Beck injury update after missing Chiefs game

Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Arizona Cardinals took the field against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 11. However, they went into this game without rookie Carson Beck under center. Veteran Josh Johnson was the starter on Sunday, with Beck sitting on the sidelines. Beck missed Sunday’s game with a back injury. Johnson took over the offense, but couldn’t lead Arizona to a win. The Chiefs won on Sunday, and Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur spoke about Beck’s injury after the loss . “They’re back spasms. There’s no magic pill you can take for that. You just treat it, and kind of go from there. Obviously kept him back for obvious reasons… We kept Carson back because we didn’t think it was beneficial for anyone to bring him here,” the Cardinals head coach said, via PHNX Cardinals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Johnson turned in a solid performance for Arizona, tossing one touchdown pass and racking up 155 yards through the air. He did not throw an interception, either. Johnson did fumble once, but it was recovered by the Cardinals. Still, Arizona had no answer for Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs offense. Mahomes threw for 324 yards while also throwing three touchdown passes. Kansas City improved to 8-2 on the season with its 34-7 victory over the Cardinals on Sunday. Arizona is looking to find some sort of positive momentum in a lost season. One thing that could swing their way is getting Beck back healthy. The Cardinals drafted him in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Seeing what he can do on the field is important for the team’s near- and long-term future. Arizona will look to get back in the win column on November 29 when they take on the Washington Commanders. top.title: Full Card Revealed For ONE Friday Fights 180 On November 27
top.description: ONE Championship closes out November with a fresh slate of martial arts action at Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand, live in Asia primetime on Friday, November 27. ONE Friday Fights 180 features nine bouts across Muay Thai, kickboxing, and MMA, with the athletes chasing the US$100,000 contract and a spot on ONE’s main roster. In the main event, Denkriangkrai Mavinn Muaythai adds another chapter to his long Lumpinee Stadium resume when he meets Myanmar’s Thway Lin Htet in a strawweight Muay Thai contest. The 27-year-old southpaw grew up training at his uncle’s gym, which was built inside a rubber plantation, and he has since become one of the most battle-tested athletes on the weekly series. A former Omnoi Stadium Champion who draws inspiration from his Team Mavinn Muaythai teammate Shadow Mavinn , he owns 10 victories in ONE and is known for a lethal left body kick and a sharp fight IQ. Most recently, he earned a unanimous decision over Abdessamie Rhenimi at ONE Friday Fights 166 . Photo credit: ONE Championship Standing across from him, the 23-year-old Thway Lin Htet is a Lethwei Champion who has built a reputation for highlight-reel finishes. He knocked out Kritpet PK Saenchai with a spinning elbow at ONE Friday Fights 112 and stopped two-time Lumpinee Stadium Muay Thai World Champion Chokpreecha PK Saenchai by second-round TKO at ONE Friday Fights 121 . The Phyo Wai Group representative arrives off a split-decision win over Xavier Gonzalez at ONE Friday Fights 170 , and his forward-marching style and explosive power make him a threat to end any night early. In the co-main event, Nuatoranee Jitmuangnon returns to ONE Friday Fights to take on Yodchanachai Tor Pitakchai in an atomweight Muay Thai bout. The 28-year-old Thai last stepped into the ONE ring at ONE Friday Fights 8 in 2023, and he comes back after more than three years away with a fresh opportunity to make his mark on the weekly series. Yodchanachai, who will be making his ONE debut, will look to make an impression in the opposite corner. top.title: Draymond Green gets into a viral social media clash with a former Sixth Man of the Year
top.description: Draymond Green gets into a viral social media clash with a former Sixth Man of the Year originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Draymond Green continues to be an interesting player because of how much he can impact the game without having the raw stats that other top players have. He is often a litmus test for gauging role players' impact and how they can affect their team's success. For the Golden State Warriors , Green has been a mainstay since he was drafted 35th overall in the 2012 NBA Draft. Since then, he has been playing a unique role for the Warriors , which has been appreciated by most people who have a deeper knowledge of basketball. However, recent times have shown that Green is a step slower, so he has drawn the ire of people in the NBA world. Draymond Green has a viral back-and-forth with former Sixth Man of the Year Eddie Johnson For a long time, Green has been an intriguing player. He has never been the most reliable scorer, but he has done his best to contribute on offense. With his superb screen-setting and solid playmaking, the Warriors have won four championships with him as one of Stephen Curry's sidekicks. It has worked out for Green because he has had a Hall of Fame-worthy career. Unfortunately, his numbers are being used as an argument against him. That is what former NBA Sixth Man of the Year award winner Eddie Johnson has brought up when considering Green's legacy as a potential Hall of Fame member. MORE: Victor Wembanyama was unsurprised by Draymond Green pushing him in the back This led to a huge back-and-forth between Green and Johnson. The former responded to Johnson's claim that Green would be an undeserving member of the Hall of Fame, which led to Johnson throwing some social media haymakers with his responses. "How do you weigh that against the individual résumés of those four guys who could actually carry a team if the star player they played with is injured? Check my resume; even I did that many times. I got more players for you if you want? Just doing my job, bro, as an analyst. Isn’t that your main job now, and basketball is only when Curry plays," Johnson responded to Green after the latter made fun of him . Based on the numbers on their tweets, it seems that people agree with Johnson. However, it will be hard to deny that Green is not a potential Hall of Fame member. Warriors head coach Steve Kerr will be the first one to campaign for that, and it will probably be deserved, especially for his impact as a four-time champion with the 21st century's arguably best team. This exchange definitely went viral on social media, but it also bled into the game later that day. Green made multiple three-pointers in the first quarter against the Boston Celtics , leading Drew Carter and Brian Scalabrine to blame Johnson for the game Green just had , as it looked like the four-time champ had something to prove. top.title: Pochettino’s Manchester United Era Has Nightmare Start
top.description: Nov 14, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino listens to the national anthem before the match against Haiti during the first leg of the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals at Nu Stadium. Pochettino is set to leave the U.S. national team to become head coach of Manchester United following the November international window. Mandatory Credit: David Santiago-Imagn Images Mauricio Pochettino’s first match as Manchester United manager ended in a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday, leaving the club still rooted near the bottom of the Premier League. United entered the game in 18th place after one win in their first 10 league matches—their worst start in 40 years. Michael Carrick had been sacked earlier in the month, and Pochettino was appointed on a deal through 2029 after finishing his duties with the U.S. national team. He arrived in Manchester only days earlier, vowing to rebuild “from scratch” and restore confidence. The Anfield debut unraveled quickly. Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute for a foul on Alexander Isak. Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free kick, and Florian Wirtz added a second minutes later. Liverpool controlled the rest of the match, with further goals from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Muñoz completing the rout. United never recovered from the early numerical disadvantage. This is kinda what it looked like… Liverpool against Manchester united Highlights pic.twitter.com/0seVpMCaDY — Troll Foot (@troll__foot) November 22, 2026 Pochettino later defended his players’ effort and rejected talk of immediate relegation, noting that the red card made the task nearly impossible. The result matched the joint-heaviest opening defeat for a United manager in the modern era. Fans at Anfield taunted the new coach with “sacked in the morning” chants barely two weeks into his tenure. The Argentine inherits a squad short on confidence and identity after years of inconsistency since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement. His high-pressing, attacking principles will take time to implement. Upcoming fixtures against Sporting in the Champions League and Brentford at home offer little respite. For now, the Pochettino era at Old Trafford is defined by the same problems that prompted his appointment: a side struggling to compete, now with a new voice but the same urgent need for results. The rebuild has begun, but the scoreboard offers little early encouragement.

top.title: Rutgers men’s soccer falls to Cornell in NCAA Tournament, ending memorable season in crushing fashion
top.description: A season filled with upset wins for the Rutgers men’s soccer team ended in heartbreaking, ironic fashion: with the Scarlet Knights being on the wrong end of a surprise result. The third-seeded Scarlet Knights suffered a 2-1 loss to six-seed Cornell in the second round of the NCAA Tournament on Sunday in Piscataway, conceding a golden goal in extra time that ended their 2026 season with a crushing loss. In what has been one of his most successful seasons in Piscataway, head coach Jim McElderry’s program defeated six ranked teams, finished third in the Big Ten regular season standings, reached the Big Ten Tournament semifinals and notched a spot in the NCAA Tournament for the first time since the 2022 season this fall. But like their last trip to the NCAA Tournament, when it lost 3-0 to Penn in Philadelphia in the first round in 2022, Rutgers (9-7-3, 6-3-1) was unable to earn a win. It marks the first time the Scarlet Knights have lost back-to-back NCAA Tournament games since the second round in 2003 and the first round of the 2006 edition. Playing in front of a healthy crowd at Yurcak Field, Rutgers got a goal from junior forward Dan Karsten, four saves from goalkeeper Rafael Ponce de Leon and finished even on shots on goal (5-5) with Cornell (15-3-1, 6-0-1). The Scarlet Knights overcame a deficit, responding to midfielder Ashton Wray’s opener within 15 minutes, then hanging on to send the game to extra time. But in the extra period, Rutgers conceded a dangerous free kick, and Ponce de Leon was unable to keep out a shot from Kasper Wollstein. Final (OT): Cornell 2, Rutgers 1. A crushing way for a memorable season to end for the Scarlet Knights. pic.twitter.com/sJuLRkye1M — Brian Fonseca (@briannnnf) November 23, 2026 The Scarlet Knights controlled the game in the opening half hour, taking the first two shots on goal of the contest. Cornell got on the front foot in the final 15 minutes of the first half, earning two free kicks and taking four shots, including a deflection from Nate Hovan that went just over Ponce de Leon’s net. nigeria.description: Climate advocates reacted with indignation on Monday to the COP31 summit ending in failure, with contentious talks collapsing over fossil fuels after the meeting in Turkey stretched into record overtime. The final agreement was rejected on Sunday in a chaotic finale to the UN climate summit that ran two days over schedule, underscoring the strains on diplomacy in an increasingly fractured world. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who urged nations to send fossil fuels “the way of the dinosaurs” during a fiery appearance at the talks, expressed deep dismay. “I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands,” the outgoing UN chief said in a statement. COP31 negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who unsuccessfully sought to broker consensus among nearly 200 nations, conceded he could not overcome what he called “unbridgeable red lines”. “Unfortunately, we were unable to reach agreement on a cover decision… And that’s disappointing. Very disappointing,” Bowen, who is Australia’s climate minister, told a throng of reporters. More than 49 hours after the summit was supposed to end, COP31 President and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum banged the gavel to conclude the marathon talks. Calls for reform Bowen said the summit backdrop was “the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory”, as soaring energy prices and fallout from the Middle East war complicated the search for unity. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, whose country co-hosted the summit with Turkey, attributed the failure of the talks to “difficult geopolitical times”. Under pressure to show progress in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal, Bowen sought an overarching “cover decision” to prove countries were still united in tackling the crisis. But his plan unravelled as familiar fault lines emerged over fossil fuels, with the EU and Saudi Arabia locking horns over the pace of the shift away from coal, oil and gas. The negotiations stalled as oil-producing states blocked any mention of phasing out fossil fuels in the final deal. “We will not endorse a cover decision… that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” said Ireland’s climate minister, Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency. “And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel.” Panama, Vanuatu and the Marshall Islands also objected and as the deal imploded, COP31 became the longest climate summit on record. Former US vice president and climate advocate Al Gore said it was “outrageous that a handful of petrostates have veto power over any mention of fossil fuels”. nigeria.title: Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29
nigeria.description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, with over 50 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. Governor Douye Diri disclosed this during a condolence visit by Vice President Kashim Shettima. Diri explained that the final casualty figure had yet to be established as efforts were still ongoing to recover the affected vessel. ﻿ He, however, said some passengers might still be trapped inside the boat. The governor described the incident as avoidable, alleging that the boat was not fit for river travel and had operated from an unauthorised loading point. He said the state government had taken responsibility for the medical bills and feeding of the survivors. Diri thanked President Tinubu for the concern shown by the Presidency since the incident occurred, particularly the Vice President’s visit to the state. He used the occasion to appeal for Federal Government support for the construction of more roads across Bayelsa, noting that improved road access would reduce the dependence of some communities on water transportation. The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw. The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, adding that the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m. The boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways, according to a preliminary police report. Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing. A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings. nigeria.title: 2027 Elections: Lagos Is The Big Deal To Me, Says Tinubu
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has described Lagos State as crucial ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to mobilise voters and ensure a higher turnout in the state. Tinubu spoke on Sunday during a prayer session at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club in Lagos, where he urged them not to generate the maximum win. “The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday. But we cannot take it for granted. You must knock on your neighbour’s door. “Tell them to get, collect their PVC,” he said. The President also urged the attendees at the prayer session that collecting the Permanent Voter Card (PVC) was essential to exercising their democratic rights. “If you are here and you don’t have PVC, you are just here for amala and ewedu,” he told those present jokingly. “If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6. And that’s what I want to ask you to exercise. ”To me, Lagos is the big deal. How can you have seven million registered voters and produce 100,000-200,000 votes? That’s failure. “Even if you win, and say, ‘A win is a win,’ no. You have to generate the maximum,” he added. ﻿ Tinubu lost the state to Peter Obi , who was then the presidential candidate of the Labour Party, despite the President’s longstanding political influence in the commercial capital where he served as governor from 1999 to 2007. According to results announced by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Obi polled 582,454 votes to defeat Tinubu, who secured 572,606 votes in the February 25, 2023 presidential election. The Peoples Democratic Party’s candidate in the election, Atiku Abubakar, came third with 75,750 votes, while Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party scored 8,442 votes. The results showed that although Tinubu won 11 of Lagos State’s 20 local government areas, Obi secured the overall victory, winning nine local government areas, including Alimosho, Ojo and Oshodi-Isolo. Lagos had 6,214,970 PVCs collected ahead of the 2023 election, the highest number recorded by any state in the country. However, only 1,335,729 votes were cast in the state, comprising 1,271,451 valid votes and 64,278 rejected ballots. Tinubu is seeking to consolidate his political support in the state as he prepares for another presidential contest in 2027, with opposition candidates, including Obi and Atiku, also in the race. nigeria.title: ‘We need to turn that anger into energy’ – Pochettino reacts to Man Utd’s 4-0 loss
nigeria.description: Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United must harness the pain from a 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool on Sunday into positive change despite feeling aggrieved by Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute red card. Pochettino’s reign got off to a nightmare start when Yoro was controversially sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak. United never recovered as Liverpool instantly took advantage when Dominik Szoboszlai smashed home the resulting free-kick. Defeat leaves United still second bottom of the Premier League and at risk of relegation from the English top flight for the first time since 1974. “It’s so painful, we feel pain for that defeat, but we need to keep the head up and translate that anger to an energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game,” said Pochettino. “We need to accept the reality and we need to be responsible. We need to be united, we need to be all together and I think we feel disappointed because it’s clear that after eight minutes, I think, the plan was in the bin.” Isak had taken a heavy touch and the ball appeared to be running through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens before contact was made by Yoro. “I’m not going to change what happened and being respectful is always important,” added Pochettino. “At the same time I need to defend my club and say what I feel. I feel like that was an action that everyone who plays football can see was clearly not a red card.” – ‘Changes the game completely’ – A repeat of United’s 7-0 thrashing at Anfield three years ago appeared on the cards when Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s lead inside 13 minutes. However, Pochettino’s introduction of Harry Maguire and switch to a back five helped stem the bleeding until teenager Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz rounded off the rout in the second half. “It hurts a lot. It’s a difficult moment for us but we are the only ones who can get out of that situation,” said United captain Bruno Fernandes, who raged against the decision to dismiss Yoro. “There are too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR taking so long to see to make a mistake like this that can change the game,” added the Portuguese international. “It’s not because of them we conceded the goal from the free-kick, but it changes the game completely.” Victory lifts Liverpool up to fourth in the table and within seven points of leaders Arsenal. Andoni Iraola savoured the adulation coming his way at full-time and believes his side should have run up an even bigger margin of victory. Isak and Bradley Barcola were guilty of wasting a number of big chances either side of half-time. “It’s difficult to enjoy in the Premier League, normally you suffer even if you win, but I think we could celebrate at half-time and enjoy it a little bit,” said Iraola. “We have missed some clear chances today. nigeria.title: CJN tasks lawyers to embrace scholarship
nigeria.description: …Commends Pinheiro’s 6 law books By Innocent Anaba LAGOS—THE Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has commended the contributions of Kemi Pinheiro, SAN, to legal scholarship and professional development, describing six publications presented in his honour as valuable resources that will enrich Nigerian jurisprudence and strengthen the intellectual foundation of the legal profession. Kekere-Ekun, who spoke, weekend, while chairing the public presentation of the books in Lagos, said the publications reflected an impressive combination of legal scholarship, practical experience and engagement with contemporary developments in the administration of justice. She noted that the collection, comprising four books authored by Pinheiro and two compilations produced in his honour, addressed significant areas of legal practice, including litigation, arbitration, insolvency, criminal law, technology and contemporary jurisprudence. According to her, the publications were not merely a collection of books assembled to commemorate an accomplished legal practitioner but works that sought to make legal knowledge more accessible and useful to those responsible for applying, interpreting and developing the law. The CJN said: “Taken together, the works reflect an engagement with important areas of legal practice and scholarship, as well as an attempt to preserve the experiences and contributions of a distinguished member of our profession.” Kekere-Ekun described ‘Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk’ as particularly significant because it offered a personal account of the experiences, encounters, challenges and defining moments that had shaped Pinheiro’s career spanning close to four decades at the Bar. She observed that memoirs of this nature were valuable because they preserved aspects of professional life that might never find their way into law reports or formal institutional records. Such accounts, she said, enabled younger practitioners to appreciate the human experiences behind professional milestones, including the uncertainties, disappointments and perseverance that often accompanied a successful legal career. The CJN also highlighted the importance of the two publications on arbitration and insolvency, particularly against the background of Nigeria’s increasingly sophisticated business environment and the need for effective legal responses to commercial transactions. , financial distress and dispute resolution. Similarly, she described Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure as an important contribution to an increasingly relevant area of law under the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020. According to her, its examination of corporate rescue, restructuring, administration and other mechanisms for addressing financial distress reflected the growing recognition that preserving viable businesses could, in appropriate circumstances, better serve creditors, employees, investors and the wider economy than immediate liquidation.

entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. entertainment.description: Five African destinations Nigerian passport holders can visit visa-free or with visa on arrival this Christmas holiday. Image: AI-generated. The group chat has the concerts, the dinners and the Detty December link-ups covered. But has anyone planned the getaway? Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Whether you are travelling solo, gathering your friends, taking the family along or joining a curated travel group, here are five destinations worth considering for your Christmas holiday. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. Nairobi gives you immediate access to wildlife at Nairobi National Park and the Giraffe Centre alongside lively restaurants and art spaces in Westlands and Karen, while longer itineraries open up classic game drives in the Maasai Mara, views of Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, and warm beach days in Diani or Watamu. Nigerian citizens enjoy visa-free entry for short stays of up to 60 days without needing a paid eTA, leaving more room in your budget for safaris and coastal stays. Rwanda Not everyone wants their year-end holiday to feel like a non-stop sprint, and Rwanda is built for travellers who prefer scenery, clean air, and an unhurried pace. Days in Kigali easily revolve around specialty coffee shops, contemporary art at Inema Arts Center, and a sobering, essential visit to the Kigali Genocide Memorial before you head out into the countryside. From the capital, you can track chimpanzees and walk above the trees in Nyungwe Forest, go on wildlife drives in Akagera National Park, or spend quiet afternoons along the shores of Lake Kivu. With 30-day visa-free entry for Nigerian passport holders, getting there is straightforward from start to finish. Mauritius Sometimes a proper Christmas break calls for leaving mainland schedules behind altogether for turquoise lagoons, catamaran cruises, and mountain trails. In Mauritius, you can base yourself around Grand Baie in the north for boat trips to Île aux Cerfs and lively beachside dinners, or head south-west toward Le Morne Brabant for coastal hikes and water sports. entertainment.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. entertainment.title: How La Roche-Posay Brought Skin Science to Over 500 Guests in Its First Living Lab Experience
entertainment.description: La Roche-Posay concluded its first Living Lab experience in Nigeria, welcoming Nigerian stakeholders to its opening party and three-day programme, held from 4 to 6 November 2026 at Oasis by The Five Palm, Victoria Island, Lagos. Inspired by the original Living Lab concept in Paris, the experience brought the science, research and expertise behind skincare closer to Nigerian consumers and healthcare professionals. It marked the brand’s first Living Lab in the country, creating a platform for more accessible conversations around skin health, dermatological innovation and everyday skincare. The experience opened with an exclusive session for healthcare professionals and invited guests before welcoming members of the public over the following two days. Each day featured three expert-led sessions exploring the role of dermatology and scientific research in advancing skin health, the wider impact of skin conditions on everyday life, and the importance of understanding product safety, tolerance and efficacy. The sessions brought together healthcare professionals and representatives from across Nigeria’s dermatological beauty and skincare community, encouraging knowledge-sharing and stronger connections between science, expertise and consumer education. Visitors explored five dedicated Innovation Corners showcasing La Roche-Posay’s Effaclar, Mela B3, Anthelios, Cicaplast and Lipikar ranges. Each space introduced visitors to specific skin concerns and the science behind the brand’s product formulations. Through interactive demonstrations and guided product experiences, guests gained a better understanding of different skin concerns and the role of targeted skincare in addressing them. At the Anthelios corner, visitors used a UV camera to see the effects of ultraviolet exposure and better understand the importance of sun protection. The Effaclar and Mela B3 spaces explored concerns including blemishes and hyperpigmentation, while the Cicaplast and Lipikar corners introduced visitors to approaches to caring for sensitive, damaged and dry skin. Beyond the Innovation Corners, visitors explored the Blue House, which presented La Roche-Posay’s history and commitment to dermatological innovation, and the Scars of Life Cinema. The cinema screened a 25-minute film exploring the physical and psychological realities of living with scars and scarring, including their impact on self-image and everyday life. Movies, as a powerful art form, present a sequence of events that allows viewers to see reflections of themselves or envision who they could become. One subject that art, particularly film, has explored is masculinity. However, this theme is often addressed subtly and can be easy to overlook, as the movies that dominate global box offices frequently focus on spectacle: fantasy, romance, adventure or others. Conversations about men, their inner lives, vulnerabilities and social roles are often not in the top circle. entertainment.title: Tochukwu Ekoh: What My Friend’s Passing Taught Me About Kindness
entertainment.description: A thoughtful young woman sits in a relaxed pose in a serene bedroom, reflecting peacefully. Photo credit: Alex Green/Pexels. I lost someone recently, and since then, I have found myself revisiting little moments, conversations and encounters I probably would not have given much thought to otherwise. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? Why did we have to start talking, sharing experiences and becoming familiar with each other again, only for him to die shortly afterwards? Why him? Why at that particular time? What was the reason for that reconnection, and why did it have to end this way? The timing of certain events leaves you with more questions than answers. sports.title: Maya Joint reveals what Serena Williams did in their match at Wimbledon that ‘surprised’ her
sports.description: Serena Williams made an incredible return to singles action at Wimbledon earlier this year. At the age of 44, Williams played her first singles match since 2022 on the grass courts of the All England Club. The American legend was pitted against Australian star Maya Joint, 24 years her junior, in the opening round of the tournament. Few were truly expecting Williams to be competitive after so long out of the sport, but the 23-time Grand Slam champion forced Joint to a decisive third set before coming up short 6-3, 6-7, 6-3. Photo by Tim Clayton/Getty Images Maya Joint reflects on her match with Serena Williams Reflecting on the match against Williams in an interview with Body and Soul , Joint said: “I was pretty nervous walking out onto that court knowing that everyone was going to cheer for her, but there were still plenty of people cheering for me, so that was nice. “Serena played better than I thought she was going to. Her movement was really good and that definitely took me a little bit by surprise.” Revealing what she said to Williams at the net after triumphing, Joint said: “I didn’t know what to say. “I panicked and just said, ‘Thank you.’ It was like, ‘Thank you for letting me breathe the same air that you breathe.’ I was just really relieved the match was over. That match was a turning point in the year. I started doing a lot better after that. “I think I got some confidence and relaxed a little bit, knowing that no match will be more difficult than that,” said Joint, who finished the 2026 season ranked 92nd in the world, having started the campaign ranked 32nd. Photo by Visionhaus/Getty Images Serena Williams results since her Wimbledon appearance Wimbledon marked the only tournament that Williams played singles at in 2026, though she continued featuring in doubles after her appearance in SW19. At the Cincinnati Open, Williams reunited with her sister Venus for the first time since the 2022 US Open. The Williams sisters, who claimed 14 Grand Slam titles and three Olympic gold medals as a duo in doubles, were competitive in Cincinnati, but ultimately lost to Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns in the opening round. Serena and Venus then teamed up at the US Open, but fell in the opening round once again. Serena also featured in Mixed Doubles at Flushing Meadows, partnering Carlos Alcaraz, and the two reached the quarterfinals.

sports.title: SEC fines Tennessee $250K after fans disrupted game vs. LSU by throwing golf balls and mustard
sports.description: Tennessee has been fined $250,000 by the Southeastern Conference for fan conduct that disrupted Saturday's game against LSU, the conference announced Sunday. Fans at Neyland Stadium threw golf balls and mustard onto the field during the fourth quarter of the No. 9 Volunteers' win over Lane Kiffin's Tigers , leading the teams to stop play for a few minutes. In a statement, the SEC said the fine was assessed due to fans "throwing debris" onto the field, interrupting the game and "endangering contest participants." The SEC appeared to justify the fine with a bylaw referring to the availability of alcohol, saying that the conference can fine the school "if cans or plastic bottles are used as projectiles or otherwise cause game management issues." The SEC could also suspended the university's ability to sell alcohol at games, though it said it does not plan to do so at this time. The choice to throw golf balls and mustard was not by coincidence: The seemingly random combination is connected to the school's history with Kiffin. Tennessee's hatred of the LSU coach stems from Kiffin's brief stint as head coach of the Vols in 2009, before he left to coach USC after just one year. In 2021, Kiffin returned to Neyland Stadium for the first time, then coaching Ole Miss. He was greeted with Tennessee fans who threw random debris, including golf balls and a mustard bottle. At SEC media days, Tennessee head coach Josh Heupel encouraged fans to reprise the moment when LSU came to Neyland. "I certainly hope our fan base hasn't cooled off," Heupel said at the time. "Whether it's the grocery stores being fully stocked with mustard, or our sports stores making sure that they've got reinforcements on the golf balls, hopefully Knoxville is ready for his arrival." A Tennessee field crew member carries a mustard bottle and golf balls off the field at Neyland Stadium. (Randy Sartin-Imagn Images) IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect / REUTERS Volunteers fans happily took on the challenge. In addition to bringing the items to throw at the LSU bench, several fans wore mustard bottles in the stands while cheering Tennessee to a 27-13 win. Kiffin, for what it's worth, took the situation in stride. "They listened to their coach," he said postgame. "I'm not being critical of him. I'm laughing at it."

sports.description: MEXICO CITY — Nick Bosa came to Mexico with an idea about when the fans here ought to make noise. Sunday night, before the 49ers and Minnesota Vikings had played a down, the fans let him know they had a pretty good handle on the timing. They waited until Bosa stepped onto the field for warmups at Estadio Banorte, better known as Estadio Azteca. Then came the boos, whistles and chants of “¡Culero!” — roughly “a–hole” in Mexican Spanish. He heard more of the same once the game got underway. Bosa had wanted the crowd to pick its spots. It picked one. Nick Bosa #97 of the San Francisco 49ers hits Kirk Cousins #8 of the Minnesota Vikings as he throws a pass in Mexico City on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Getty Images For a guy who plays for what felt like Mexico City’s favorite team Sunday night, that took some doing. Bosa managed it earlier in the week when he got to talking about the crowd at the 49ers’ last game here, in 2022. What the San Francisco defensive end remembered was the chanting. What he wanted this time was a little help for the home team, or at least the team that figured to feel most at home. Fair enough. Then he kept talking. “Yeah, I kind of want, I think we need some information given to the fans, so they know when to cheer,” Bosa said. “Because they just chant the whole time. If we can kind of teach them, no offense to them and their soccer cheering techniques, but if they can cheer when we’re on defense, that would be great.” Fans cheer during the first half of an NFL football game between the Minnesota Vikings and San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There’s a good football point in there. Get loud enough when the Vikings have the ball and it gets harder for their offensive linemen to hear the snap count. Ask any 49ers fan in Santa Clara to lend Bosa a hand with that and odds are they’d be happy to oblige. It was the offer to teach that got him in trouble. American football has been played in Mexico for years. In fact, Mexico City fans were packing Estadio Azteca for NFL games before Bosa was born. In 1994, 112,376 showed up to watch the Cowboys play the Houston Oilers – in the preseason. The league puts its Mexican fan base at 40 million nationwide, its largest outside the U.S. That’s the crowd Bosa offered to teach when to cheer. You can imagine how the folks who grew up watching it here felt about a visiting player offering pointers on how to root for a team plenty of them have loved longer than he’s played for it. United entered the game in 18th place after one win in their first 10 league matches—their worst start in 40 years. Michael Carrick had been sacked earlier in the month, and Pochettino was appointed on a deal through 2029 after finishing his duties with the U.S. national team. He arrived in Manchester only days earlier, vowing to rebuild “from scratch” and restore confidence. The Anfield debut unraveled quickly. technology.description: Researchers have found new ways to evade China’s Great Firewall after spending just $1 worth of tokens. That result appeared last week in a paper titled “CircumVolve: Automated Discovery of Censorship Evasion Strategies Using Large Language Models” presented at the Conference on Computer and Communications Security run by the Association for Computing Machinery’s Special Interest Group on Security, Audit and Control. Penned by six researchers from the University of Massachusetts Amherst, University of Colorado Boulder, and activist group the Great Firewall Report, the paper points out that finding holes in the Great Firewall is a laborious process – so just the kind of task worth handing to AI. The authors came up with a tool they call “CircumVolve” and describe as “a system for automated discovery of censorship circumvention strategies across the full network stack.” “CircumVolve combines LLM code generation with iterative feedback-driven evaluation to produce verifiable and deployable evasion techniques,” they wrote. “CircumVolve models different censorship techniques as discrete scenarios, each capturing the specific context, protocol constraints, and blocking mechanisms of real-world censors. Within each scenario, evasion strategies are represented as executable Python programs that implement packet and protocol manipulations — from rewriting TCP/IP header fields, to crafting DNS queries that exploit parser ambiguities, to modifying the internal structure of encrypted QUIC Initial packets — while maintaining protocol correctness within tolerable bounds or strategically violating it when beneficial.” The authors tested CircumVolve on simulated censorship tools used by China, Iran, Pakistan, and Kazakhstan, and on virtual private servers deployed on clouds in those countries. Those tests found the median API cost to the first successful evasion was less than $1 in token expenditure costs when using GPT-5.1. The authors acknowledge that operators of censorship infrastructure might be able to observe CircumVolve at work, but feel its relatively small payloads – 80 KB of outgoing and 150 KB of incoming traffic – and 25-45-second pauses between tests might see it fly under the radar. “CircumVolve represents a first step in leveraging LLMs to accelerate the censorship-circumvention lifecycle,” the authors wrote. “By automating the labor-intensive tasks of protocol analysis, implementation, and testing, AI-driven approaches make studying circumvention capabilities far more accessible to the comparatively under-resourced Internet freedom community [and] demonstrates how AI-assisted systems can narrow the resource gap between Internet freedom advocates and well-funded censoring states.” Lenovo finally cracks monster datacenter profits Ever since acquiring IBM’s x86 server business in 2014, Chinese hardware giant Lenovo has struggled to turn a profit from datacenter sales, even as it expanded its business into storage, networking, and selling to hypersc

science.title: Watch live on Nov. 23: Amazon launching 1st batch of internet satellites since Vulcan Centaur failure
science.description: null Another batch of Amazon internet satellites will fly on Monday morning (Nov. 23), just eight days after a launch failure doomed 40 of the spacecraft. An Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation is scheduled to lift off from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana on Monday, during a 29-minute window that opens at 6:09 a.m. EST (1109 GMT; 8:09 a.m. local time in Kourou). You can watch it live here at Space.com, courtesy of Arianespace, the French company that operates the Ariane 6. Coverage will begin about 30 minutes before launch. An Ariane 6 rocket launches 32 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit from French Guiana on Feb. 12, 2026. (Image credit: ESA/CNES/Arianespace-ArianeGroup/Optique Video du CSG-P. Piron) Amazon Leo, so named because it will operate in low Earth orbit , will compete with SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 operational spacecraft. Amazon's network will eventually have more than 3,200 satellites, but just 400 or so have reached orbit to date. Another 40 were supposed to be delivered on Nov. 15, but they were lost after their rocket ride, a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur , suffered a problem shortly after launch. Ariane 6 and Vulcan Centaur aren't the only rockets Amazon is depending on to build its broadband constellation. Jeff Bezos' company has also booked rides on ULA's Atlas V rocket, Blue Origin's New Glenn and SpaceX's Falcon 9 . Vulcan will be grounded for a while as ULA investigates the Nov. 15 failure and works to fix whatever caused it. And New Glenn hasn't flown since April, when the rocket failed to deliver AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite to the proper orbit. New Glenn's return to flight was further complicated on May 28, when the rocket exploded during a routine prelaunch test. The Ariane 6, the successor to Arianespace's Ariane 5 heavy lifter, debuted in July 2024 and has nine launches under its belt to date. All of them have been successful except that maiden mission, which was a partial failure. Monday's mission will be the fourth Amazon Leo flight for the Ariane 6, following launches in February, April and June of this year.

science.title: 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson
science.description: 7 Min Read 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson NASA astronaut Randy Bresnik, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano, former NASA astronaut Russell “Rusty” Schweickart, and NASA astronauts Frank Rubio and Bob Hines appear onstage at the Artemis Celebration Gala at the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Merritt Island, Florida, on Nov. 6, 2026. Credits: Purpose Entertainment/Shanna Lockwood Employees and guests of NASA’s Johnson Space Center celebrate the center’s 65th anniversary at the Lunar Receiving Park in Houston on Nov. 19, 2026. NASA/Robert Markowitz For 65 years, NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston has helped shape human spaceflight, from the Gemini missions that demonstrated rendezvous and docking techniques needed for Apollo to the research conducted aboard the International Space Station, which has supported a continuous human presence for more than 26 years. Today, Johnson teams are preparing crews and systems for NASA’s next chapter: returning astronauts to the lunar surface and building the capabilities needed for a long-term human presence at the Moon. Across those missions, generations of flight controllers, engineers, scientists, instructors, medical specialists, and other experts have helped crews live and work beyond Earth. Johnson is home to NASA’s Orion and Moon Base programs, and its teams continue to support space station operations, astronaut training, spacecraft development, mission operations, and human health. Mercury and Gemini: Preparing for Apollo When the Manned Spacecraft Center officially opened on Nov. 1, 1961, NASA had already flown two suborbital Mercury missions, with the first orbital flight just months away. Most Project Mercury activities remained at Cape Canaveral in Florida to maintain continuity, but the new Project Gemini took up residence in Houston, housed in temporary leased facilities across the city while construction of the new Clear Lake campus continued. The new Mission Control Center became NASA’s primary flight control center in June 1965, with the Gemini IV mission that included the first American spacewalk. Houston became the nerve center for American human spaceflight, overseeing the remaining eight Gemini missions before transitioning to the Apollo program. Following the tragic Apollo 1 fire in January 1967, managers, engineers, and astronauts at the Manned Spacecraft Center applied lessons learned to make the spacecraft safer and ensure the safety of its astronauts, resuming crewed missions in October 1968. Managers in Houston devised a daring plan to send Apollo 8 on a circumlunar flight. In December 1968, Apollo 8 made its historic trip around the Moon, and seven months later Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Edwin “Buzz” Aldrin landed on the lunar surface. Their first voice transmission back to Earth after their arrival began with the word “Houston.” Five more Moon landings completed the Apollo program and humanity’s first phase of lunar exploration

science.title: SpaceX sends classified US spy satellites to orbit in early-morning launch from California coast (video)
science.description: null SpaceX launched a batch of classified satellites this morning (Nov. 22), on the NROL-136 mission out of California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Launch Complex-4E at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California). It was the sixth National Reconnaissance Office launch (NROL) this year to deliver a payload, or group of payloads, to low Earth orbit , all which have been carried out by SpaceX 's workhorse Falcon 9. The launch marks another step in the NRO's effort to expand its intelligence-gathering capabilities through a proliferated network of spacecraft designed to provide more frequent and timely surveillance of locations around the globe. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the NROL-136 mission for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office from California on Nov. 22, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) About two minutes after liftoff, the Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued carrying the classified payloads onward to orbit. The booster then reversed course and returned to Vandenberg, touching down at Landing Zone 4 approximately seven and a half minutes after launch. Saturday's launch was the 14th flight for this particular Falcon 9 booster, dubbed B1097, which previously launched NASA 's Sentinel-6B ocean-monitoring satellite, NROL-172, USSF-259 for the U.S. Space Force , and eight Starlink missions. NROL-136 is the 15th launch dedicated to building the NRO's "proliferated architecture," the satellites for which have been developed in partnership with SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The network is designed to increase coverage and improve the "capability and resilience" of U.S. intelligence operations in space , according to the NRO's mission website . The NRO began deploying the constellation in May 2024 with the launch of NROL-146. The most recent proliferated architecture mission before Sunday was NROL-179, which lifted off on June 19, 2026. As with any classified mission, the agency has not disclosed the exact number of satellites aboard NROL-136 or revealed details about their onboard technologies.

With the sad passing of its star, Patrick Stewart , last month, and "Star Trek's" milestone 60th birthday taking place in 2026, this is a bittersweet salute that also holds an extra special significance. Directed by "The Next Generation's" Number One, Jonathan Frakes , in his feature film debut, " First Contact " consistently ranks as one of the finest "Star Trek" feature films among fans and critics, and those accolades are well deserved. Based on a compelling screenplay by Brannon Braga and Ronald D. Moore, "First Contact" remains as bright and beautiful as ever, brimming with bravado, heart, horror, and heroism. Not only was it a bona fide crowdpleaser when it was released by Paramount over Thanksgiving week on Nov. 22, 1996, but it was also a financial success for the studio, eventually pulling in a worldwide total of $212 million off a modest $45 million budget. science.description: null On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered From its start, the Space Transportation System, better known as the space shuttle, was a compromise between meeting civilian and military needs. NASA saw the vehicle as a means of supporting science research, establishing an on-orbit economy (servicing commercial satellites and flying company payloads) and ultimately, assembling the parts for a space station. The Department of Defense saw the shuttle as an asset to deploying and retrieving reconnaissance satellites, among other projects, some of them classified. It was not until the loss of the space shuttle Challenger, that it was decided that the shuttle would only be used by the military when it was key to national security. Other needs would be met by expendable launch vehicles (ELVs). As an aside, the STS-33 astronauts also spent Thanksgiving in space during this mission. But the holiday was off to a crappy start when the shuttle's toilet broke first thing in the morning. After spending most of the day fixing it, they got to enjoy their Thanksgiving turkey together. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong? I've chased eclipses long enough to know that the celestial mechanics are the easy part. The moon will arrive exactly on schedule — that's guaranteed. Everything else — the weather, the crowds, the transport, the equipment and the people — is rather less predictable. From the possibility of dust storms to uncertainty about whether boats will even be allowed to move on the Nile, there are plenty of reasons to be slightly wary about what awaits eclipse chasers after the ultimate bragging rights on Aug. 2, 2027. Here are the 10 things worrying me most about the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt. A dust storm could make the eclipsed sun less impressive. (Image credit: Grant Faint via Getty Images) 1. A sudden dust storm The chances of cloud-free skies in Luxor and anywhere in Upper Egypt in August are exceptionally high — close to 100%. That's almost unheard of in eclipse-chasing. However, clouds aren't the only thing that can obscure the sun. Dust and sand are potential hazards in the Egyptian desert, and a dust storm at the wrong moment could affect—though probably not ruin—the view. Although the sun will almost certainly be visible during the eclipse, airborne dust could hide the delicate structure of the solar corona. 2. In 2027, however, the city and its surrounding urban area — population about four million — could swell as eclipse chasers, tour groups, photographers and curious visitors descend. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."
